reasoning_trace.description: The paper proposes a novel deep learning-based method called SDOA-Net for direction of arrival (DOA) estimation in imperfect arrays, which takes raw sampled signals as input and produces a vector that can be used to estimate the spatial spectrum.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper presents a system model for practical DOA estimation, considering various imperfect factors such as antenna position perturbations, inconsistent gains and phases, mutual coupling effects, and nonlinear effects. The proposed SDOA-Net method uses convolution layers to extract features from the raw sampled signals and achieves faster convergence in training compared to other deep learning-based methods.

reasoning_trace.description: The system mechanism and ISAC coupling mode are based on a deep learning approach, utilizing a convolutional neural network (CNN) to estimate the DOA.
reasoning_trace.value: The SDOA-Net method uses a CNN architecture with multiple convolution layers, followed by batch normalization and ReLU activation functions. The output of the network is a vector that can be used to estimate the spatial spectrum, which is then used to determine the DOA.

reasoning_trace.description: The physical consistency of the reported metrics is verified by comparing the performance of the proposed SDOA-Net method with existing methods such as MUSIC, ANM, FFT, and OMP.
reasoning_trace.value: The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SDOA-Net method outperforms existing methods in terms of DOA estimation accuracy, especially in scenarios with imperfect arrays. The method achieves a 39.13% improvement in RMSE compared to the ANM method at an SNR of 10 dB.

reasoning_trace.description: The solved problems and remaining open challenges are identified, including the improvement of DOA estimation performance in imperfect arrays and the development of more efficient and robust methods.
